title: Live Ninja — User Settings (v1)
description: Canonical per-user settings document. Stored as DynamoDB item PK=USER#<userId> SK=SETTINGS (see PRD.md §8.1). Top-level values are the account defaults shared by web, Android, and M5Stack; deviceOverrides contains sparse per-device section overrides in the same document and under the same optimistic-concurrency version. Every reader/writer, including firmware written years apart, MUST preserve unknown fields on write-back per contracts/README.md rule 2. additionalProperties is true at every object level for exactly this reason.

version.description: Optimistic-concurrency counter (FR-S01). Every PUT/UpdateItem carries ConditionExpression version = expected and increments this on success; a stale write gets HTTP 409 and the client re-reads/re-applies. This is NOT a schema version — schema evolution is additive-only per contracts/README.md and is not tracked by this field.

wakeWord.description: ID of the active wake-word catalog entry (FR-K02). Always a combobox selection over the shared catalog + the user's own trained models — never a free-typed phrase. Resolves via GET /v1/wakeword catalog and the per-user WAKE# items; the actual model asset is fetched via contracts/wakeword-manifest.md.

wakeEngine.description: Wake-word inference engine backing the selected wakeWord (FR-K02, FR-M02). `openwakeword` is the free/default engine (Android FGS, web WASM). `porcupine` is the optional Picovoice engine (Android; requires an AccessKey — reveals that field via progressive disclosure, UX-R05). `wakenet` is the M5Stack ESP-SR primary on-device engine (FR-M02); M5Stack falls back to an oWW-ESP model when a custom phrase isn't available as a curated WakeNet model (FR-K05).

sensitivity.description: Wake-word detection sensitivity, always a bounded slider — never a text field (FR-K06).

persona.description: Persona selection (FR-S03). Sent/stored as a catalog ID; the server resolves the actual system instructions server-side (anti prompt-injection — clients never send raw instructions to the realtime broker). `presetId: "custom"` is the sole justified free-text case (UX rich-UI case 6): it reveals `systemInstructions` as a capped, labeled editor with reset-to-preset.

presetId.description: Catalog persona ID (e.g. "default") or the literal "custom".

systemInstructions.description: Free-text system-instruction override. Only meaningful/editable when presetId == "custom"; null/absent otherwise. Capped length enforced server-side (see api.md PUT /v1/settings validation).

hidden.description: Persona IDs the user has switched OFF in the picker (owner request 2026-08-01). Presentation only: it hides entries from the persona pickers and NOTHING else — the server's ResolvePersona deliberately ignores it, so a stale client, another device, or a persona still referenced by presetId always resolves to a working session. Opt-OUT by design: a new built-in appears automatically rather than needing to be enabled, which an allow-list would get backwards. "default" may never appear here; it is the fallback that guarantees the picker is never empty.

voice.description: Account-wide FALLBACK OpenAI Realtime voice, chosen from an enumerated picker — never free text. Personas are the unit of voice identity: per-persona voice lives in `personaPrefs` and wins over this field at mint (voice = personaPrefs[persona].voice ?? persona's suggested voice ?? this field ?? cedar). Default is `cedar` per PRD Q-14. New voice enum members may be appended in later milestones per contracts/README.md rule 3; an unrecognized value on read must fall back to `cedar` in the UI but be preserved verbatim on write-back.

keepListeningSeconds.description: How long the web client keeps the session live and the mic listening after a completed reply before ending the conversation itself. 0 (default) = no client-side timeout: the mic keeps listening until the user ends the conversation or the voice provider closes the session (owner decision 2026-07-19 — the provider owns session end). Non-zero values end the session that many seconds after the last reply (the pre-M13 hardcoded behavior was 10). In hands-free/wake-word mode the mic mutes during this window and the wake phrase resumes it; the same timeout (or none, for 0) applies to the muted wait.

geminiVoice.description: Account-wide Gemini Live voice for the gemini-flash-live engine (M13, D4), chosen from the enumerated `geminiVoices` catalog on GET /v1/realtime/voices — never free text. The OpenAI `voice`/`personaPrefs` values are meaningless on Gemini, so this is a separate field; at mint the broker resolves geminiVoice = this field ?? the persona's hand-curated Gemini voice ?? Kore. "" means unset (fall through the chain). Optional; absent normalizes to "". Unrecognized values must be preserved on write-back but fall through the chain at mint (forward-compat, contracts/README.md rule 3).

voiceAccent.description: Account-wide FALLBACK speech-accent directive id, chosen from the enumerated accent picker (GET /v1/realtime/voices `accents` catalog) — never free text. Per-persona accent lives in `personaPrefs` and wins over this field at mint (accent = personaPrefs[persona].accent ?? this field). Accents are not separate voices: the realtime voice set is fixed, so the broker appends a short speech-style directive (e.g. "Speak with a light, natural Irish accent.") to the session instructions at mint. "" (also surfaced as catalog id "none") means no directive. Optional; absent normalizes to "". Unrecognized values must be preserved on write-back but mint without an accent (forward-compat, contracts/README.md rule 3).

personaPrefs.description: Per-persona voice identity ("we need a persona, not a voice"): map of personaId -> {voice, accent, updatedAt}. Keys are the same ids `persona.presetId` stores — built-in catalog ids, the user's own custom-persona ids, shared-catalog ids, or the literal "custom" — never server-composed mint refs. At mint the broker resolves voice = personaPrefs[persona].voice ?? the persona's suggested voice ?? top-level `voice` ?? cedar, and the accent directive from personaPrefs[persona].accent ?? top-level `voiceAccent` (an entry whose `accent` is present-but-"" means EXPLICITLY no accent). Top-level voice/voiceAccent remain only as the account-wide fallback default. MIGRATION: on read, a stored document that predates this field seeds personaPrefs[persona.presetId] once from the top-level voice/voiceAccent, preserving the user's current sound for their current persona. Capped at ~200 entries — the server prunes oldest-`updatedAt` entries beyond the cap on write. Optional; absent normalizes to {}. Unknown per-entry fields are preserved on write-back (contracts/README.md rule 2).

voice.description: Realtime voice id for this persona (same value space as top-level `voice`). Unrecognized values are preserved on write-back and fall through the mint precedence chain.

accent.description: Accent directive id for this persona (same value space as `voiceAccent`; "" = explicitly no accent, overriding the top-level fallback).

updatedAt.description: RFC3339 UTC timestamp of the last edit — the prune-oldest ordering key for the ~200-entry cap.

turnDetection.description: Turn-detection strategy bound into the realtime session config at mint (FR-V01, PRD §6.2). Exposed to the user as a radio control (UX-R01/R02). `semantic_vad` is the platform default and pairs with `interrupt_response:true`.

theme.description: UI theme, segmented control (UX-R02). `light` is the app-zone default look (ninja-light); the live panel's chrome comes from appearance.liveStyle, not from this axis.

micDeviceId.description: Selected input device id from the browser's enumerateDevices()/Android getAvailableCommunicationDevices() (UX-R01) — populated control, never typed. Null means "system default device".

voiceEngine.description: Voice-engine selection (FR-VE-01..04). In account defaults, `default` is the inherited engine. In a deviceOverrides.voiceEngine section, `default` is that device's effective engine. `devices` is the deprecated pre-M31 per-device pin map retained additively for old clients; readers use it only when the corresponding device has no voiceEngine section override, and section writes migrate/clear its entry. `nova-sonic` reintroduces a backend media bridge for ONLY a selected device (FR-VE-04) — all other engines stay client-direct.

devices.description: Deprecated M12–M30 map of deviceId -> pinned engine. Preserved for compatibility; new clients use deviceOverrides[deviceId].sections.voiceEngine.

privacy.description: Retention/storage controls (FR-S04). Included here because Settings is the one canonical doc (FR-S01) and these fields gate DynamoDB TTL + S3 lifecycle enforcement; not in the required core list above because it predates no milestone dependency, but MUST be present on every settings document the server writes at account-creation time.

storeAudio.description: Persist raw audio to S3 (opt-in). Off by default — on-device wake + this flag are the load-bearing privacy controls (PRD §10).

retentionDays.description: TTL window for transcripts/logs. Radio control, not free text (FR-S04).

micEagerness.description: Mic pickup: how quickly semantic VAD treats a pause as end-of-turn (maps to the realtime API's turn_detection.eagerness). Optional; absent normalizes to auto.

appearance.description: Visual customization across two style zones plus a global accent color. `appStyle` styles everything OUTSIDE the conversation page's live panel (the ninja navy-and-teal app chrome); `liveStyle` styles the conversation page's live panel (orb/mic rail — hal9000 red glowing eye by default). `accentColor` "" means each zone uses its style's own default accent. Optional; absent normalizes to the defaults. MIGRATION: the pre-split single `themeStyle` (which styled the conversation orb/mic panel) migrates to `liveStyle` on read/write and the deprecated key is dropped.

appStyle.description: Style zone for everything outside the live panel (the app chrome).

liveStyle.description: Style zone for the conversation page's live panel (orb/mic rail).

accentColor.description: #rrggbb, or empty string for each zone's style default accent.

deviceOverrides.description: Sparse per-device settings. Keys are owned DEVICE ids, never client-supplied hostnames or hardware identifiers. Each entry contains only sections customized for that device; a missing device or section inherits the corresponding top-level account defaults. The section PATCH API owns mutation of this map so clients cannot overwrite another device accidentally. `Apply to all` updates the top-level defaults and removes the understood fields in that section from every device entry while retaining additive fields from newer clients. Legacy clients that do not know this field preserve it verbatim.

profile.description: Base Knowledge profile (M15). This top-level value is the account default; a deviceOverrides.aboutYou section may customize it for one named host. The effective profile is injected server-side into every minted session's instructions as a BASE KNOWLEDGE block (internal/realtime/baseknowledge.go) and used as the default argument source for profile-aware tools (get_weather location/units, scheduler timezone). This is deliberately NOT the memory layer: memory is episodic and retrieval-on-demand, this is stable and always-present. Locations are stored GEOCODE-VERIFIED — lat/lon/timezone are resolved at save time via GET /api/v1/geocode, never at question time. Optional; an absent or empty profile mints exactly as before. M16 adds a refinement loop on top: the assistant's profile_suggest tool and the tool-failure RCA analyzer PROPOSE changes as separate PROFSUGG# items (not part of this document), which the owner approves in Settings. Only `units` and a `notes[]` addition are eligible for legacy account-default auto-apply (see those fields), and named-device invocations leave those pending for an explicit scoped choice; displayName, pronouns, contactEmail, locale, homeLocation and workLocation always require confirmation.

displayName.description: What the assistant calls the user. Free text by necessity (rich-UI case 6 — a personal name is genuinely unconstrained).

pronouns.description: Optional. Rendered into the base-knowledge block so the model refers to the user correctly.

homeLocation.description: Default location for weather, time, and anything else location-shaped. When set, get_weather needs no location argument at all and skips the geocoding leg entirely.

workLocation.description: Optional second known place, same shape as homeLocation.

units.description: Unit system for temperature, wind, distance. Becomes the default `units` argument for get_weather. One of the only two fields eligible for the legacy account-default M16 auto-apply policy: the value set is enumerable, the effect is immediately audible in the next answer, and Settings shows an Undo. A named-device invocation leaves it pending for an explicit scoped choice. Everything else needs the owner's confirmation.

locale.description: BCP-47 locale tag (e.g. en-US). Optional; informs number/date phrasing in the base-knowledge block.

contactEmail.description: The user's own email address, so the assistant can say where a deliverable went without asking. NOT an authorization grant — send_email still enforces the owner-managed allow-list server-side.

quietHours.description: Optional local-time window during which the assistant should avoid proactive contact. Both fields are 24h HH:MM.

notes.description: Short free-form owner facts that belong in every effective session profile but aren't a modeled field — the 'everything else' bucket. Capped so the instruction block can't grow without bound. The other field eligible for the legacy account-default M16 auto-apply policy, and only ever by ADDING an entry the user spoke explicitly — never by replacing the list; Settings shows an Undo that removes exactly the entry that was added. A named-device invocation leaves it pending for an explicit scoped choice.

sections.description: Section-keyed sparse overrides. Values use the same top-level field names and shapes as the canonical document. Known section ids are aboutYou, wakeWord, persona, voiceEngine, turnDetection, appearance, microphone, and privacy; unknown future sections must be preserved.

updatedAt.description: Server-written time of the most recent override change for this device.

deviceSection.description: A sparse section payload whose keys are canonical top-level settings fields. Unknown fields are retained for additive schema evolution.

profileLocation.description: A geocode-verified place. Written only from a GET /api/v1/geocode selection (house UI rule: known-value fields are pickers, never blind text boxes), so lat/lon/timezone are always resolved and trustworthy. null = not set.

label.description: Human-readable resolved label shown back to the user, e.g. "Huntersville, North Carolina, United States".

admin1.description: State / province / region as returned by the geocoder.

timezone.description: IANA timezone id (e.g. America/New_York) resolved by the geocoder. Drives the local date/time line in the base-knowledge block and the default timezone for scheduler tools.
